predecessors.note: The Rudrama Devi page: Amba-deva 'carved out an independent principality that included almost all of the former south-western parts' of the Kakatiya territory 'to the south of the Krishna River'. The start year is the latest bound ('before 1281'); Ambadeva became chief in 1272. Nellore is not part of the land: it was a Telugu Choda throne under Ambadeva's nominee (vassal events).

land.text: the Kadapa country and Mulikinadu, annexed in 1309 ('The region was annexed to the Kakatiya kingdom', Prataparudra II page); Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre

successors.note: The Tripurantakam area had passed to the Kakatiyas in 1291 and Nellore in 1290. Who held the Kadapa core between 1291 and 1309 (Ambadeva himself, Tripurari-deva II or another Kayastha chief) is on no page opened.

capitals.name: Valluru-pattana
capitals.note: 'He made Valluru-pattana his capital, and strengthened the hill fort of Gandikota-Monrathapura' (Ambadeva page). The page does not say where Valluru-pattana is; the point is Proddatur (heart of Renadu, Renadu page) as a stand-in, so the dot is only good to a county. Gandikota is at 14.815N 78.287E in Kadapa district (Gandikota page). The page names the capital but not the year it was chosen, so 1281 is the state's start.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks. The Ambadeva page lists the principality in the 1287 Attirala inscription as 'his capital Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva, and Pottapi-nadu', which is the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema (Renadu page: the heart of Renadu is Proddatur, Jammalamadugu and Nandyal); the pages give no boundaries, so the shape is a 90 km radius round Proddatur plus a 40 km radius round Tripurantakam, where Ambadeva's 1273 and 1290 inscriptions stand. The 40 km Tripurantakam area is lost in 1291 (ledger). Nellore is not part of the shape: Manuma Ganda-gopala held it under Ambadeva (vassal events). An earlier draft drew Ongole 120 km plus Nellore 100 km, which no page supports. Confidence is low.

ledger.note: before 1281: Ambadeva rules an independent Kayastha principality south of the Krishna. The Rudrama Devi page has him become chief in 1272, initially loyal but later asserting independence, and install Manuma Ganda-gopala on the Nellore throne 'Sometime before 1281'; the Ambadeva page says 'soon asserted independence', lists the principality in the 1287 Attirala inscription and has the 1290 Tripurantakam inscription 'practically proclaim Amba-deva's sovereignty' (he is allied with the Pandyas and Seunas 'By 1290'). No page dates the independence, so 1281 is the latest date by which it is attested (confidence 1); the Ambadeva page itself says 'before 1282'.

ledger.note: before 1281: the principality takes the Kadapa country and the Tripurantakam area out of the Kakatiya kingdom (kakatiya-dynasty carries the matching loss). The Rudrama Devi page has Ambadeva carve it out of the 'former south-western parts' of the Kakatiya territory south of the Krishna. Nellore is no longer part of this gain: it was in Telugu Choda hands (Tiru-kalatti-deva II 'apparently ruled Nellore during c. 1279-1283, before another Choda chief Manuma-Gandagopala displaced him').

region.text: Nellore, where Ambadeva had appointed Manuma Ganda-gopala to the throne (a vassal, not Ambadeva's own land)

ledger.note: before 1281: Ambadeva's nominee holds Nellore. 'Sometime before 1281, Amba-deva appointed Manuma Ganda-gopala on the throne of Nellore' (Rudrama Devi page; the Ambadeva page says before 1282, from Manuma's 1284 Kodavaluru inscription). The page calls Manuma 'another Choda chief', so the counterpart is the Telugu Chodas of Nellore (a dossier from sa-03-x is wanted). Year is the page's latest bound.

region.text: Nellore, where Ambadeva had appointed Manuma Ganda-gopala to the throne (a vassal, not Ambadeva's own land)

ledger.note: 1290: the Kakatiyas defeat Manuma Ganda-gopala and take Nellore. 'In 1290 CE, Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore.' An earlier draft had c. 1298, the year of a 1297-98 inscription on the Prataparudra II page (the second expedition, against Raja-Gandagopala's alliance with the Pandyas); the Ambadeva page's 1290 replaces it. kakatiya-dynasty carries the matching gain.

region.text: the Kadapa country and Mulikinadu, to which Ambadeva 'had to retreat southwards' from Tripurantakam (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

ledger.note: 1291: Prataparudra's army marches on Ambadeva. 'In 1291-92 (Shaka 1213), Prataparudra sent an army to Tripurantakam' and 'Ambadeva had to retreat southwards to the Mulikinadu region' (Prataparudra II page). Rudrama had been 'killed in November 1289 CE by Amba-deva's forces' (Rudrama Devi page). No page records fighting between 1291 and 1309; the contest is kept open to the 1309 expedition because the Kayastha rule lasted until then.

ledger.note: mid-1291: Ambadeva loses Tripurantakam. A Kakatiya force 'defeated him in mid-1291'; his 'last record at Tripurantakam is dated 13 June 1291' and 'the earliest record of Manuma-Gannaya and Annaya-deva at the place is dated 11 August 1291' (Ambadeva page). The page does not give a month. kakatiya-dynasty carries the matching gain.

The year is the page's; the drawn region is the Kadapa country, which is my reading of the Mulikinadu the page names, so confidence 2.

wars.outcome: Ambadeva, chief from 1272, asserted independence, killed Rudrama in November 1289 (a theory on indirect evidence), lost Nellore (his nominee Manuma-Gandagopala) to Prataparudra in 1290 and Tripurantakam in mid-1291, and lost Mulikinadu to the Kakatiya expedition of 1309.
wars.note: Prataparudra II page: the army sent to Tripurantakam in 1291-92, Ambadeva's retreat 'southwards to the Mulikinadu region' and the end of Kayastha rule in 1309. Ambadeva 'defeated Shripati Ganapati of Gurindala' in 1273 (Rudrama Devi page).

certainty.note: The pages name places and inscription find-spots, not borders; the shape is two radii.

notes: Written by the sa-03-h agent as a rebel state of its own states' wars (no Cliopatria row); repaired on 2026-10-19 after review, with the Ambadeva article opened. The principality was the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema (the 1287 Attirala inscription's list: Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva, Pottapi-nadu) plus the Tripurantakam area until mid-1291, with its capital at Valluru-pattana; Nellore was a Telugu Choda throne under Ambadeva's nominee Manuma Ganda-gopala, a vassal relation and not Ambadeva's land. Dates: chief 1272; Nellore nominee 'before 1281' (Rudrama Devi) or 'before 1282' (Ambadeva); independence undated, 1281 is a bound; the 1290 Tripurantakam inscription 'practically proclaims' sovereignty; Nellore lost 1290; Tripurantakam lost in mid-1291 (13 June to 11 August); Mulikinadu annexed 1309. Not on any page opened: Ambadeva's death, and who held the Kadapa core between 1291 and 1309 (the Ambadeva page offers Tripurari-deva II as a ruler who 'may have ruled the territory lost by Amba-deva'; the Prataparudra II page speaks of 'Kayastha rule' to 1309). Valluru-pattana is not located on any page; the capital dot is Proddatur as a stand-in. Gazetteer names wanted: Tripurantakam (place), Valluru-pattana (place), Gandikota (place), Kadapa/Cuddapah (place), Mulikinadu and Renadu (regions).
